coachMessages.text: In Connect Four, odd rows belong to Red, even rows to Yellow. The first piece in any column goes to row 0, the bottom row — Red's row.

slides.infoProse: The bottom row (row 0) belongs to Red because Red always plays first. Yellow gets row 1, Red gets row 2, and so on. This bottom-up alternation is called parity and it never changes.

coachMessages.text: Gravity means pieces fill from the bottom. Red gets row 0, Yellow row 1, Red row 2 — bottom-up parity is locked.

slides.infoProse: With three discs stacked in column 3, the alternating parity is clear: Red (bottom), Yellow (middle), Red (top). Every piece obeys this bottom-up rule.

coachMessages.text: Understanding which rows belong to which player is the foundation for Claimeven, Z-Threats, and all advanced tactics.

slides.infoProse: Mastering parity is what separates beginners from advanced players. Every fork, threat, and blockade traces back to this one idea.
